sink: id is concatenated raw into the REST path passed to plankaRequest(), which builds the final URL with `new URL(path, baseUrl)`; WHATWG URL dot-segment resolution lets a value like "../projects/<targetId>" strip the "/api/boards" prefix and retarget the request at a completely different Planka resource (e.g. /api/projects/<targetId>) while keeping the caller-chosen HTTP method (DELETE for delete_board).
why: index.ts:41-161 passes args.id straight to boards.deleteBoard/updateBoard/getBoard with no format check; common/utils.ts:110-112 builds the URL via native `new URL()`, which normalizes ".." segments per RFC3986 before the request is sent, so id="../projects/X" turns a delete_board call into a DELETE against /api/projects/X. No encodeURIComponent, UUID regex, or path allow-list exists anywhere in the repo (grepped for encodeURIComponent/uuid/sanitize/validateId with zero hits) and the DELETE path never validates the response shape, so the request completes regardless.
contract: Manage projects and boards with various operations
